title: Training Note — The Payment Due for the Cycle on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans
content:
# Training Note — The Payment Due for the Cycle on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

*Basis questions answered for the finance desk.*

**What is the payment due for a cycle on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan?** It is read in one of three ways, according to what the whole month ending on the handling date holds.

- Where a payment on the plan has been sent back unpaid in that month, the payment due is the scheduled monthly payment the plan record carries together with the money sent back unpaid in that month.
- Where no payment has been sent back unpaid and a settled payment stands in that month, the payment due is what is left of the scheduled monthly payment after the settled payments credited in that month, never less than nothing.
- In every other case, the payment due is the scheduled monthly payment the plan record carries.

**Which reading governs where the month holds both a return and a settled payment?** The first. A payment sent back unpaid in the month fixes the reading whatever else the month holds, so the money sent back is added to the scheduled monthly payment rather than the settled payment being taken off it.

**Can the second reading fall below nothing?** No. Settled payments in the month larger than the scheduled monthly payment leave a payment due of nothing, never a negative figure.

## The three readings on hypothetical figures

A plan record carries a scheduled monthly payment of 180.00 USD.

| What the whole month ending on the handling date holds | The payment due |
|---|---|
| A payment of 180.00 USD sent back unpaid | 180.00 USD together with 180.00 USD, that is 360.00 USD |
| A settled payment of 120.00 USD and no return | 180.00 USD less 120.00 USD, that is 60.00 USD |
| A settled payment of 200.00 USD and no return | Nothing, the settled payment exceeding the scheduled monthly payment |
| Neither a return nor a settled payment | 180.00 USD |
